title: 4GE1-style exam questions: energy demand, sources and sustainable management (Paper 2, Topic 4.3)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 30 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 30: Revision: energy demand, sources and sustainable management (Paper 2, Topic 4.3). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Evaluate the management of energy resources in a developed and a developing or emerging country.' Portal response box.
questions.a: Two named countries; strategies (mix, renewables, efficiency, imports); successes and problems with evidence; comparison; substantiated judgement
questions.model: Teacher plans: P1 developed country (for example the UK: coal phased out, more wind) with evidence; P2 developing or emerging country with evidence; P3 compare; conclusion.

questions.q: Make a two-minute verbal summary of Paper 2 Section A topics for a partner (breakout room).
questions.a: Accurate summary of urban and economic activity and energy content

questions.q: Explain why some countries keep using coal despite its impacts.
questions.a: Cheap and plentiful domestic supply (1); reliable for industry (1); jobs depend on it and renewables need investment (1)

questions.q: Explain one reason why energy demand is rising in emerging economies.
questions.a: Industrialisation (1) increases energy use in factories; rising incomes mean more cars and appliances (1)
questions.model: Cause: industry grows and people earn more. Effect: factories, cars and appliances use more energy. So demand rises.

questions.q: State one disadvantage of wind power.
questions.a: Intermittent: no electricity when the wind does not blow (or visual impact)

questions.q: Give one benefit of a diverse energy mix.
questions.a: Greater energy security: less reliance on one source

questions.q: Big question: can the world have enough energy without harming the planet?
questions.a: Reasoned view: possible with efficiency, conservation and a fast shift to renewables, but costly and uneven between countries
